items.prompt: A notification service must create an EmailSender, SmsSender or PushSender based on the user's preference string; plugins add new channels.
items.why: Choose which concrete class to instantiate from a key, extensible → factory with a registry.

items.prompt: An HTTP request object has a method, URL, optional headers (repeatable), optional query params, an optional body and a timeout; some combinations are invalid (GET with a body).
items.why: Many optional/repeatable parts + cross-field validation before use → Builder.

items.prompt: Your app must run on two clouds. For each cloud you need a matching storage client, queue client and secrets client — never mixing clouds.
items.why: A *family* of related products that must match → Abstract factory.

items.prompt: Unit tests for `OrderService` are flaky because it calls `Database.get_instance()` internally and tests share data through it.
items.why: The deciding signal is the hidden dependency that tests can't replace. That's DIP: inject the database instead of reaching for a global singleton.

items.prompt: A legacy `XmlInvoiceReader` has `parse_file(path)`, but the new pipeline expects every reader to implement `read(stream) -> Invoice`.
items.why: Making an existing class fit another interface is Adapter. Nothing new is being chosen or created.

items.prompt: A `DataImporter` base class runs validate → transform → save; each subclass needs to supply its own parser object to the first step.
items.why: The base workflow asks subclasses which product to create → Factory method.

items.prompt: Checkout must apply one of several discount rules, chosen per campaign and changed at runtime by marketing.
items.why: The variation is behaviour after construction → Strategy. A factory could produce the rule, but that isn't the core of the question.
